title: Postmortem: RBAC policy deployment caused authorization failures (2026-03-18)
author: Naomi Feldman
content:
## Summary
On 2026-03-18, a production RBAC policy deployment caused increased authorization failures for Console and API key management operations. The issue was triggered by a deny rule that unintentionally matched a broad set of service principals.

## Customer impact
- Duration: 29 minutes
- Symptoms: users unable to rotate API keys; some Console pages failed to load; elevated 403s
- Scope: Primarily enterprise orgs using fine-grained role assignments

## Detection
- Alert: authz-service 403 anomaly
- Support escalation: enterprise admins unable to manage keys

## Timeline (UTC)
- 09:14: 403 anomaly alert fired
- 09:18: Security on-call begins investigation
- 09:27: Mitigation: rollback RBAC bundle to previous version
- 09:43: Error rates return to baseline

## Root cause
A deny rule intended to restrict a deprecated permission used a wildcard principal selector. During compilation, the selector expanded to include internal service principals used by Console and key management workflows. The policy review process did not include a compilation preview step.

## Contributing factors
- Lack of policy compilation preview in CI
- Incomplete test coverage for key management operations under enterprise RBAC configurations

## Follow-up action items
1. Add CI step to compile RBAC policies and produce a diff of effective principals/permissions for reviewer approval. Owner team: Security. Priority: P0.
2. Add integration tests covering API key rotation and Console admin flows under restricted enterprise policies. Owner team: Platform. Priority: P0.
3. Add a staged rollout mechanism for RBAC bundles with automatic rollback on 403 anomaly. Owner team: Platform. Priority: P1.
4. Update security runbook to include "403 anomaly" triage steps and safe rollback procedure. Owner team: Security. Priority: P1.

## Lessons learned
Policy-as-code needs the same rigor as application code: previews, diffs, tests, and staged rollouts with automatic rollback.
